finding.claim: Unauthenticated insecure deserialization: the /restore endpoint passes a client-supplied, base64-decoded parameter directly to Marshal.load. A crafted Marshal gadget chain (for example the well-known Ruby universal deserialization gadgets) gives remote code execution on the server.
finding.source: HTTP POST /restore, form/query parameter `state` (params[:state]), fully attacker-controlled, no authentication required

trace.note: post "/restore" route is exposed with no authentication or authorization filter
params[:state] is Base64-decoded, which only changes the encoding and does not validate the content
Marshal.load deserializes arbitrary Ruby objects, so gadget chains run during deserialization
state.inspect is reached only if load succeeds, and the payload has already executed by then

finding.guards_checked: No authentication, signature/HMAC, class allowlist, or safe-loader is used. There are no before filters or middleware in this file, and the file contains no Sinatra settings. Sinatra's default Rack::Protection does not stop this. The only other non-trivial endpoint, /import, uses JSON.parse, which is not exploitable for object injection, so it is not reported.

verdict.reason: app.rb:6 passes Base64.decode64(params[:state]) straight into Marshal.load on the unauthenticated post "/restore" route (app.rb:5). app.rb is the only file in the directory, so there is no auth, signature, allowlist or middleware, and Marshal.load on attacker-controlled bytes is a known RCE sink.

verdict_facts.reason: app.rb:5-6 exposes POST /restore with no auth filter, and Marshal.load(Base64.decode64(params[:state])) deserializes attacker-controlled data with no signature, allowlist or safe loader, and app.rb is the only file in the directory.
